column1: # Coverage register — a recorded reason for every gap the audit tolerates.
#   "what" is a method name, or the source text of a partially-covered condition.
#   It is deliberately NOT a line number: lines move, and a register keyed on them
#   goes stale on the first unrelated commit and silently stops matching.
#   tier:integration     needs Docker; a test tier covers it, the hermetic gate cannot
#   tier:ml              needs a trained model artifact
#   tier:live            needs the network or a plugin jar on disk
#   terminal             needs a real TTY (JLine raw mode / keystroke dispatch)
#   framework-override   an @Override this codebase never calls; a framework does
#   entry-point          a process entry point, covered by the packaging smoke tests
#   unreachable          no supported input reaches it — the reason must say *why*
# A row here is a claim that the gap is not worth closing, and it is reviewed like
# any other claim. "Hard to reach" is not a reason; "the grammar cannot express it"
# is. Adding a row to silence the audit without a reason that survives reading is
# the one thing this file is meant to prevent.

EXPR-001 has already folded it. accumulateConstants has one caller, simplifyBinary, which passes it children that are ALREADY simplified; outerOp is restricted to PLUS/MULTIPLY and inner.operator() == outerOp, so the inner is never the DIVIDE that EXPR-001 declines to fold. An inner with two numeric-literal children therefore cannot survive to reach this guard — it was folded to a single NumberOperand on the way in, and `left instanceof BinaryArithmeticExpression` then fails one line earlier.

The mirror of the guard above, unreachable for the same reason: EXPR-001 folds two adjacent numeric literals under a commutative operator before accumulateConstants is ever reached, so the inner expression cannot hold two of them.

The OUTER arm has no surface syntax: docs/reference/operators/unnest.md records the OUTER variant of μ as programmatic-only, so no script can produce an UnnestNode with outer=true. The ordinality half of the same condition IS reachable and is covered by MongoPushdownPlannerTest.ordinalityUnnestIsNotPushed.

topK()'s clause-order guard sits below a `!node.groupingAttributes().isEmpty()` bail, and the grammar REQUIRES the PER clause (docs/reference/advanced/top.md), so every written TOP bails before reaching it. The empty-PER TopKNode that gets here is built only by LimitPushdownPass when a λ folds over a τ — an optimizer-produced shape this text-driven pushdown harness does not run. PlannerTest is where it would arrive.

The alias is always a declared source name, and the grammar cannot produce a non-identifier one. base() sets `alias = node.name()` only after sources.get(name) found a declaration, and parseSourceDeclaration takes its name from requireName(), which accepts an IDENTIFIER or a keyword-used-as-identifier — both lexed as a word, the same character class this pattern tests. Backtick-delimited names belong to the expression grammar and are rejected in a source declaration. Kept as belt-and-braces: the alias is emitted unquoted into the FROM clause, so the check is cheap insurance against a future name rule that admits more.
The mirror of the guard above, unreachable for the same reason: both aliases come from declared source names, which the grammar guarantees are identifier-shaped.
an abstract holder of static factories — nothing constructs it and nothing can; it is a class only so ScriptBuilders can extend AstBuilders and serve the whole authoring surface from one import

the no-solver message, thrown when SolverCatalog.installed() finds none; relix-solver-ojalgo is a provider on every test classpath, so this constructor always finds one — the no-solver behaviour is asserted at the planner instead, where it is raised before any input is read

converts a closed row arriving under an OPEN output heading — reachable only for WHY over a schema-on-read source, whose connector (json/http) lives in relix-connectors-std, above this module; every open-schema row this module can produce is already a DocumentRow
'join is missing its condition' — the planner only chooses HASH for a join that has one; a conditionless join is a product, which takes a different arm entirely
'NTILE requires a bucket-count argument' — RelAlgebraValidator rejects an NTILE without one before a plan exists, so the executor cannot be handed a validated plan that lacks it
'Unknown relation in query target' — a named query target that resolves to nothing is a semantic error, so analysis fails before a model reaches the executor
asserts an ImportGraph invariant — processingOrder() lists keys of the very map script() reads, so this fires only on a defect inside ImportGraph rather than on any input

one iterator cannot outlast the other here. The loop is reached only once the degrees compare equal, and it returns the moment an entry differs — so exhausting i while j has entries left would mean every compared entry was identical and j still holds variables with exponents the constructor guarantees are positive, making other's degree strictly the larger. The degrees were equal, so that cannot happen: the loop always ends with both exhausted, which is also why the size tie-break below it always answers 0.

an overload map is never empty while it exists. registerFunction creates it with computeIfAbsent immediately before an unconditional put, and its one early return happens only when an overload was already present; no method on this table removes an entry or a map. Kept as belt-and-braces rather than simplified to a null check: without it an empty map would break the namespace fall-through early and return no function at all, so the guard is what makes the invariant safe to be wrong about.

the right half cannot be true here. EMPTY-003 rewrites `X ⊎ ∅` to X, bottom-up, before this classifier is asked about the node — from the pass's own walk or from an operator above it — so every ⊎ that survives to be classified has a live right branch, and the second call answers false whenever the first was true. The arm is written symmetrically with ∪/⊔/∆ beside it because the law is the same; only ⊎ has a rule that gets there first.

syntaxDiagnostic has one caller, validate(String), and its parse() runs ScriptParser — which raises ScriptParseException and places every failure it raises. Both false arms therefore describe inputs no frontend on this path produces. A cause that is not a ScriptParseException would be a parser defect rather than a rejected script: parse() catches RuntimeException deliberately widely so that one is reported to the caller as a diagnostic instead of escaping validate(), which is documented as the one method that does not throw. A ScriptParseException with line() == 0 is the core-level contract for a frontend with no line/column notion — a builder API — and such a frontend hands the session a Script rather than text, so it never reaches parse() at all.
